chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abdullah ibn Muskan and Muhammad ibn al-Nu'man al-Ahwal from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When a traveler joins a group of residents in their prayer, if it is the first prayer (Dhuhr), he should make the obligatory part within the first two rak'ahs; and if it is Asr, he should make the first two rak'ahs voluntary (nafl) and the last two obligatory."
ai.seo_question: How should a traveler perform prayer when joining a resident congregation for Dhuhr or Asr?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific mechanism for *Jam' al-Ta'khir* (delayed combination) when a traveler joins a resident congregation, distinguishing between Dhuhr and Asr to ensure the obligatory count is met within the four-rak'ah structure. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on maintaining the integrity of the four-rak'ah prayers (Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib) even during travel, provided the traveler aligns their intention with the congregation's rhythm. This ruling highlights the practical flexibility granted to travelers while preserving the communal aspect of prayer.
